3) **Drawing:** Produce $PA$ to $D$ such that $PA = AD$. Add $Q, D$.

**Proof:**

In triangle $\triangle QAD$ and $\triangle PAR$,
$QA = AR, AD = PA$
and the included $\angle QAD = $ the included $\angle PAR$
$\therefore \triangle QAD \cong \triangle PAR$ and $QD = PR$
Now, in $\triangle PQD, PQ + QD > PD$
or, $PQ + PR > 2PA$ [$\because A$ is the mid point of $PD$]

Similarly, $PQ + QR > 2QB$ and $PR + QR > 2RC$
$\therefore PQ + PR + PQ + QR + PR + QR > 2PA + 2QB + 2RC$
or, $2PQ + 2QR + 2PR > 2PA + 2QB + 2RC$
or, $PQ + QR + PR > PA + QB + RC$
$\therefore PA + QB + RC < PQ + QR + PR$
